linear.start: Look for {{target}} among {{count}} values, from left to right.
linear.compareNo: Is items[{{i}}] = {{value}} equal to {{target}}? No, keep going.
linear.notFound: Reached the end without finding {{target}}. Return -1. Comparisons made: {{comparisons}}.

bubble.start: Sort {{count}} values by swapping neighbours that are out of order.
bubble.pass: Pass {{pass}}: compare neighbours from index 0 up to index {{end}}.
bubble.compareSwap: Compare items[{{j}}] = {{a}} and items[{{k}}] = {{b}}: {{a}} > {{b}}, so they are out of order.
bubble.compareKeep: Compare items[{{j}}] = {{a}} and items[{{k}}] = {{b}}: already in order, leave them.
bubble.swap: Swap them, so the larger value {{a}} moves right: {{list}}.
bubble.passEnd: End of pass {{pass}}: {{value}} has bubbled up to index {{end}}, its final place.
bubble.earlyExit: No swaps in pass {{pass}}: everything is already in order, so stop early.

selection.start: Sort {{count}} values: each pass finds the smallest remaining value and puts it next in line.
selection.pass: Pass {{pass}}: fill index {{i}}. Start by assuming items[{{i}}] = {{value}} is the smallest.
selection.compareNew: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} smaller than the smallest so far, {{b}}? Yes!
selection.compareKeep: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} smaller than the smallest so far, {{b}}? No.
selection.newMin: Remember the new smallest: {{value}} at index {{j}}.
selection.swap: Swap it into index {{i}}: {{value}} is now in its final place: {{list}}.
selection.inPlace: {{value}} is already at index {{i}}, so no swap is needed.

insertion.start: Sort {{count}} values like cards in your hand: take each one and slide it left into place.
insertion.pick: Pass {{pass}}: lift out key = items[{{i}}] = {{value}}. Index 0..{{last}} is already sorted.
insertion.compareShift: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} bigger than the key {{value}}? Yes: it must shift right.
insertion.compareStop: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} bigger than the key {{value}}? No: stop here.
insertion.reachedStart: Reached the start of the list: {{value}} is the smallest so far.
insertion.shift: Shift {{a}} one place right. The gap is now at index {{gap}}.
insertion.insert: Drop the key {{value}} into the gap at index {{pos}}: {{list}}.

merge.start: Sort {{count}} values by splitting the list in half until each piece has one value, then merging the pieces back in order.
merge.mergeStart: Merge {{left}} and {{right}}: point a finger at the start of each half.
merge.rest: One half is used up: copy the leftovers {{rest}}.

quick.start: Sort {{count}} values: pick a pivot, move smaller values to its left and larger ones to its right, then sort each side.
quick.partition: Partition index {{lo}}..{{hi}} around the pivot {{pivot}} (the last value).
quick.compareSmall: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} ≤ the pivot {{pivot}}? Yes: it joins the small side.
quick.compareBig: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} ≤ the pivot {{pivot}}? No: it stays on the big side.
quick.swap: Swap {{a}} into index {{i}}, the end of the small side.
quick.placePivot: Put the pivot {{pivot}} at index {{p}}: smaller values are left of it, larger ones right. It is in its final place.
quick.single: Only {{value}} is left in this range: it is in its final place at index {{p}}.

heap.start: Sort {{count}} values with a heap: a tree stored in the list, where every parent is at least as big as its children.
heap.build: Phase 1: build a max-heap. Sift down every parent, starting from the last one at index {{k}}.
heap.pickTwo: Children of index {{root}} are {{a}} and {{b}}: the bigger one is {{c}} at index {{child}}.
heap.pickOne: Index {{root}} has one child: {{c}} at index {{child}}.
heap.heapOk: Parent {{v}} ≥ child {{c}}: this part of the heap is fine, stop.
heap.swapDown: Parent {{v}} < child {{c}}: swap them, so {{c}} moves up.
heap.leaf: Index {{root}} has no children left to check: stop.
heap.sortPhase: Phase 2: the biggest value is at the top. Move it to the end, shrink the heap, and repair it.
heap.extract: Swap the top {{max}} with the last heap value: {{max}} is now in its final place at index {{end}}.

counting.start: Sort {{count}} small whole numbers without comparing them: count how many of each there are, then write them out.
counting.makeCounts: The largest value is {{k}}, so make {{size}} counters, all starting at 0.
counting.tally: items[{{p}}] = {{x}}: add one to count[{{x}}], which is now {{c}}.
counting.write: count[{{value}}] = {{c}}: write {{value}} out {{c}} time(s). Result so far: {{list}}.
counting.done: Sorted: {{list}}. Each of the {{n}} values was counted once and written once, with no comparisons.

radix.start: Sort {{count}} values digit by digit, without comparing them: first by the ones digit, then by the tens digit.
radix.pass: Pass for the {{digit}} digit (place = {{place}}): start with 10 empty buckets, 0 to 9.
radix.drop: {{x}}: its {{digit}} digit is {{d}}, so it goes into bucket {{d}}.
radix.collect: Collect the buckets from 0 to 9, keeping each bucket's order: {{list}}.
radix.done: place = {{place}} is bigger than the largest value {{max}}, so stop. Sorted: {{list}}.

form.start: Start with (up to {{max}} values, may be empty)

error.empty: Enter at least one operation. Commands: {{help}}
error.tooManyOps: Use at most {{max}} operations. Small examples are easier to follow.
error.unknown: I don't know the command “{{command}}”. Commands: {{help}}
error.badStart: “{{token}}” isn't a value here. Use whole numbers from -99 to 99, or single letters.
error.badCapacity: Capacity must be one whole number from 2 to 8.
error.badNumber: “{{token}}” isn't a number. This structure orders its keys, so use whole numbers from -99 to 99.
error.emptyStart: Start with at least one value.
error.badCount: The number of items must be one whole number from 2 to 8.
error.badVertex: Enter one vertex to start from, for example A.

graph.help: add u v, remove u v, has u v, neighbours u

preset.square: A square, then remove an edge

graph.emptyGraph: No vertices yet. Add an edge to start.
graph.start: An empty undirected graph. It is shown three ways: as a picture, as an adjacency list and as an adjacency matrix.
graph.addNew: Add edge {{u}}–{{v}} (new vertex: {{fresh}}). Each list gets the other vertex; the matrix gets two 1s.
graph.add: Add edge {{u}}–{{v}}. Each list gets the other vertex; the matrix gets two 1s.
graph.selfLoop: {{u}}–{{u}} would link a vertex to itself, which this graph doesn't allow.
graph.matrixYes: Matrix: row {{u}}, column {{v}} holds 1, so yes. One lookup, no matter how big the graph is.
graph.matrixNo: Matrix: row {{u}}, column {{v}} holds 0, so no. One lookup.
graph.listYes: List: scan {{u}}'s neighbours {{list}}: found {{v}} after {{checks}} check(s).
graph.listNo: List: scan {{u}}'s neighbours {{list}}: no {{v}} after {{checks}} check(s).
graph.removed: Remove edge {{u}}–{{v}} from both lists and both matrix cells.
graph.removeMissing: {{u}}–{{v}} isn't an edge: nothing to remove.
graph.neighbours: {{u}}'s neighbours: {{list}} (degree {{deg}}). The list has them ready; the matrix would scan all {{n}} cells of row {{u}}.
graph.end: {{n}} vertices, {{e}} edge(s). The list stores {{listSize}} entries (V + 2E); the matrix stores {{matrixSize}} cells (V²).

recursion.help: factorial n, total n (n from 0 to 7)
recursion.start: Each call gets its own frame on the call stack, with its own n. A call waits until the call it made returns.
recursion.call: {{name}} isn't a base case, so it needs {{next}}: call it. Stack depth {{depth}}.
recursion.base: {{name}} is the base case: it returns {{value}} straight away, without calling again (depth {{depth}}).
recursion.return: {{name}} gets {{r}} back and returns {{n}} {{op}} {{r}} = {{value}}. Its frame is removed.
recursion.result: {{name}} = {{value}}. The stack grew to {{depth}} frame(s), then emptied as each call returned.
recursion.end: Every frame waited for the one above it, then returned in reverse order: last in, first out, like a stack.

hanoi.start: Move {{n}} disk(s) from peg A to peg C, one at a time, never putting a bigger disk on a smaller one. It takes at least {{min}} moves.
hanoi.move: The {{below}} smaller disk(s) that were on top of it are parked on {{spare}}, so disk {{disk}} can move from {{source}} to {{target}}. (Move {{moves}}.)
hanoi.qPeg: Disk {{disk}} leaves {{source}}. Which peg does it go to?
hanoi.done: All {{n}} disk(s) are on C after {{moves}} moves: 2ⁿ − 1, so each extra disk doubles the work.

bfs.help: A B (an edge between A and B), e.g. A B, A C, B D
bfs.missingStart: {{s}} isn't in the graph. Add an edge that uses it.
bfs.start: Start at {{s}}: mark it seen and put it in the queue.
bfs.visit: Take {{v}} from the front of the queue and visit it. Order so far: {{order}}.
bfs.seen: {{w}} has already been seen: skip it.
bfs.enqueue: {{w}} is new: mark it seen and add it to the back of the queue {{queue}}.
bfs.endAll: Queue empty: every vertex was visited, nearest first. Order {{order}}.
bfs.endSome: Queue empty. Order {{order}}. Never reached: {{missed}} (no path from the start).

dfs.help: A B (an edge between A and B), e.g. A B, A C, B D
dfs.missingStart: {{s}} isn't in the graph. Add an edge that uses it.
dfs.seen: {{w}} has already been visited: skip it.
dfs.deeper: {{w}} is new: go deeper from {{v}} to {{w}}.
dfs.back: {{v}} has no unvisited neighbours left: back up to {{parent}}.
dfs.doneRoot: {{v}} has no unvisited neighbours left: the search is complete.
dfs.endAll: Every vertex was visited, going as deep as possible first. Order {{order}}.
dfs.endSome: Order {{order}}. Never reached: {{missed}} (no path from the start).

topo.help: a > b (a must come before b), e.g. wake > dress
topo.start: Count each task's prerequisites (in-degree). Tasks with none are ready: {{ready}}.
topo.decrement: {{w}} needed {{v}}; it still waits for {{d}} more.
topo.nowReady: {{w}} needed {{v}}, its last prerequisite: {{w}} is now ready.
topo.endAll: Every task is placed after its prerequisites: {{order}}.
topo.cycle: Nothing is ready, but {{left}} are left: they wait on each other in a cycle, so no order exists. Placed: {{order}}.

dijkstra.help: A B 4 (an edge A–B of length 4), e.g. A B 4, A C 1
dijkstra.missingStart: {{s}} isn't in the graph. Add an edge that uses it.
dijkstra.start: Every distance starts at ∞, except {{s}} = 0. Put (0, {{s}}) on the heap.
dijkstra.settle: The closest unsettled vertex is {{v}} at distance {{d}}: its distance is now final.
dijkstra.stale: ({{d}}, {{v}}) is out of date: {{v}} was already settled at {{best}}. Skip it.

kruskal.help: A B 1 (an edge A–B of weight 1), e.g. A B 1, B C 2
kruskal.start: Sort the edges by weight: {{sorted}}. Take the cheapest edge that doesn't close a loop.
kruskal.take: {{u}} and {{w}} are in different pieces: take it. Total weight {{total}}.
kruskal.skip: {{u}} and {{w}} are already connected: {{u}}–{{w}} would close a loop, so skip it.
kruskal.end: Done: {{count}} edges connect all {{n}} vertices with total weight {{total}}.
kruskal.endForest: The graph isn't connected: {{count}} edge(s) join what can be joined (total {{total}}).

unionFind.help: union a b, find a, connected a b
unionFind.start: {{n}} items, 0 to {{last}}, each in its own group: parent[i] = i.
unionFind.hop: {{x}} isn't a root: go up to its parent, {{p}}.
unionFind.root: {{root}} is its own parent, so it is the root (the group's name) for {{x}}.
unionFind.compress: Path compression: point {{nodes}} straight at {{root}}, so the next find is one hop.
unionFind.attach: Different groups: attach root {{small}} under root {{big}} (the bigger group). The group now has {{size}} item(s).
unionFind.sameSet: {{a}} and {{b}} already share root {{root}}: nothing to join.
unionFind.qConnected: Are {{a}} and {{b}} in the same group? (✓ yes / ✗ no)
unionFind.connectedYes: Both have root {{ra}}: {{a}} and {{b}} are connected.
unionFind.connectedNo: Roots {{ra}} and {{rb}} differ: {{a}} and {{b}} are not connected.
unionFind.badItem: Item {{x}} doesn't exist: items are 0 to {{last}}.
unionFind.end: {{n}} items in {{sets}} group(s). With union by size and path compression, each operation is nearly O(1).

traversal.start: A binary tree of {{count}} nodes, filled level by level. Each traversal visits every node once, in a different order.
traversal.preorderStart: Pre-order: visit the node first, then its left subtree, then its right subtree.
traversal.inorderStart: In-order: left subtree first, then the node, then the right subtree.
traversal.postorderStart: Post-order: both subtrees first, the node last.
traversal.levelorderStart: Level-order: row by row from the top, using a queue.
traversal.end: Each traversal visited all {{count}} nodes exactly once: O(n).

bst.help: insert k, search k, delete k (whole numbers)
bst.start: In order: {{list}} ({{n}} nodes). Smaller keys go left, larger keys go right.
bst.qSide: From {{v}}, does {{k}} go left (←) or right (→)?
bst.createRoot: The tree is empty: {{k}} becomes the root.
bst.createLeft: Empty spot: {{k}} becomes the left child of {{parent}} (depth {{depth}}).
bst.createRight: Empty spot: {{k}} becomes the right child of {{parent}} (depth {{depth}}).
bst.duplicate: {{k}} is already in the tree, so nothing changes.
bst.searchMiss: Reached an empty spot: {{k}} is not in the tree ({{comparisons}} comparison(s)).
bst.deleteMiss: {{k}} is not in the tree: nothing to delete.
bst.deleteLeaf: {{k}} has no children: simply remove it.
bst.deleteOneChild: {{k}} has one child, {{child}}: the child takes its place.
bst.deleteTwo: {{k}} has two children. Replace it with its successor: the smallest key in its right subtree.
bst.succStart: Step into the right subtree: start at {{s}}.
bst.succLeft: Go as far left as possible: {{s}}.
bst.copySucc: {{s}} is the successor: copy it into {{k}}'s place.
bst.removeSucc: Remove the old {{s}} node (it has no left child). In order: {{list}}.
bst.end: {{n}} node(s), height {{h}}. A search takes at most {{h}} comparison(s).

avl.start: An AVL tree with {{n}} node(s), height {{h}}. The number under each node is its balance: left height minus right height.
avl.qSide: From {{v}}, does {{k}} go left (←) or right (→)?
avl.duplicate: {{k}} is already in the tree, so nothing changes.
avl.create: Insert {{k}} as a new leaf. Now walk back up and check each balance.
avl.unbalanced: {{v}} has balance {{b}}: too lopsided, so rotate.
avl.caseLL: Left-left case at {{v}}: one right rotation fixes it.
avl.caseRR: Right-right case at {{v}}: one left rotation fixes it.
avl.caseLR: Left-right case at {{v}}: first rotate {{c}} left, then rotate {{v}} right.
avl.caseRL: Right-left case at {{v}}: first rotate {{c}} right, then rotate {{v}} left.
avl.rotatedChildLeft: After the left rotation, {{top}} is on top of that subtree.
avl.rotatedChildRight: After the right rotation, {{top}} is on top of that subtree.
avl.rotatedRight: Rotated right: {{top}} moves up. Every balance is back between -1 and +1.
avl.rotatedLeft: Rotated left: {{top}} moves up. Every balance is back between -1 and +1.
avl.end: {{n}} node(s), height {{h}}, in order {{list}}. AVL keeps the height near log₂ n.

heap.start: Min-heap {{list}}: every parent is ≤ its children, so the smallest value is at index 0.
heap.append: Append {{x}} at index {{i}}, the next free spot.
heap.swapUp: Parent {{pv}} > {{x}}: swap, so {{x}} moves up to index {{p}}.
heap.reachedTop: {{x}} reached the top: it is the new minimum.
heap.qSettle: At which index does {{x}} end up?
heap.peek: heap[0] = {{top}} is the smallest value. No work needed.
heap.qTop: Which value is at the top?
heap.top: The top, {{top}}, will be returned. Take the last value off the end.
heap.moveLast: Put {{last}} at the top, then sift it down.
heap.end: Heap: {{list}}. Each insert or extract followed one path: O(log n).

trie.help: insert word, search word, prefix p (letters only)
trie.start: An empty trie. Each node is one letter; a ringed node ends a word.
trie.markWord: Mark the last node: "{{word}}" ends here.
trie.missing: No '{{ch}}' child: "{{word}}" isn't in the trie.
trie.searchHit: The last node is marked: "{{word}}" is a word in the trie.
trie.searchPrefixOnly: The path exists but isn't marked as a word: "{{word}}" is only a prefix.
trie.end: {{count}} word(s) in {{nodes}} letter node(s): {{words}}. Shared prefixes are stored once.

segment.help: sum l r, set i x
segment.start: {{n}} values. Each node stores the sum of its range; the root holds the total, {{total}}.
segment.take: [{{lo}}..{{hi}}] is inside {{l}}..{{r}}: take its whole sum {{sum}} (running total {{total}}).
segment.split: [{{lo}}..{{hi}}] partly overlaps {{l}}..{{r}}: look at both halves.
segment.badRange: The range {{l}}..{{r}} isn't valid: use 0 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ {{last}}.
segment.goLeft: {{i}} is in the left half of [{{lo}}..{{hi}}]: go left.
segment.goRight: {{i}} is in the right half of [{{lo}}..{{hi}}]: go right.
segment.end: Total: {{total}}. Queries and updates each touched about 2 × log₂ n nodes.

hashTable.help: insert k, lookup k, delete k
hashTable.start: {{m}} empty buckets. A key goes into bucket hash(key) % {{m}}.
hashTable.hashLetter: hash('{{k}}') = ord('{{k}}') % {{m}} = {{code}} % {{m}} = {{b}}: go straight to bucket {{b}}.
hashTable.scanNo: {{e}} is not {{k}}: check the next key in this chain.
hashTable.alreadyThere: {{k}} is already in bucket {{b}}, so nothing changes.
hashTable.collision: Collision! Bucket {{b}} already holds a key, so {{k}} joins its chain (now {{size}} long).
hashTable.lookupHit: Found {{k}} in bucket {{b}} after {{checks}} check(s). The other buckets were never looked at.
hashTable.lookupMiss: {{k}} is not in bucket {{b}}, so it is not in the table ({{checks}} check(s)).
hashTable.deleteFound: Found {{k}} in bucket {{b}}: remove it from the chain.
hashTable.deleted: {{k}} removed from bucket {{b}}. No other key moved.
hashTable.deleteMiss: {{k}} is not in bucket {{b}}: nothing to delete.
hashTable.end: {{n}} key(s) in {{m}} buckets: load factor {{load}}, longest chain {{longest}}. Short chains keep every operation fast.

hashSet.help: add x, contains x, remove x
hashSet.start: {{m}} empty buckets. A value goes into bucket hash(value) % {{m}}.
hashSet.hashLetter: hash('{{k}}') = ord('{{k}}') % {{m}} = {{code}} % {{m}} = {{b}}: go straight to bucket {{b}}.
hashSet.scanNo: {{e}} is not {{k}}: check the next value in this bucket.
hashSet.alreadyThere: {{k}} is already in the set, so it is not added again.
hashSet.collision: Bucket {{b}} already holds a value, so {{k}} joins it (now {{size}} in this bucket).
hashSet.lookupHit: contains({{k}}) is True: found in bucket {{b}} after {{checks}} check(s).
hashSet.lookupMiss: contains({{k}}) is False: it is not in bucket {{b}}.
hashSet.deleteMiss: {{k}} is not in the set: nothing to remove.
hashSet.end: The set holds {{n}} distinct value(s) in {{m}} buckets (load factor {{load}}).

probing.start: {{m}} empty slots. A key starts at slot key % {{m}}; if that slot is taken, try the next one.
probing.occupied: Slot {{i}} holds {{v}}, not {{k}}: move on to slot {{next}}.
probing.store: Slot {{i}} is empty: store {{k}} there ({{probes}} probe(s)).
probing.lookupEmpty: Slot {{i}} is empty, so {{k}} can't be further along: not found ({{probes}} probe(s)).
probing.full: OverflowError: all {{m}} slots are taken, so {{k}} can't be stored.
probing.lookupFullMiss: Checked all {{m}} slots: {{k}} is not here.
probing.end: {{n}} key(s) in {{m}} slots: load factor {{load}}. As it gets close to 1, probe runs get long.

array.help: read i, insert x at i, delete i, search x
array.start: a = {{list}}: {{count}} values in neighbouring boxes. Each box is 4 bytes, starting at address 100.
array.read: a[{{i}}]: jump straight to address 100 + {{i}} × 4 = {{addr}} and read {{value}}. No scanning needed.
array.insertError: Can't insert at index {{i}}: the list only has {{n}} values (valid: 0..{{n}}).
array.grow: Make room: the list grows to {{n}} slots, with an empty slot at the end.
array.write: Write {{x}} into the gap at index {{i}}. Inserting here moved {{moved}} value(s).
array.deleteStart: Delete index {{i}} (value {{value}}): it leaves a gap.
array.shrink: Drop the empty last slot: {{list}}. Deleting moved {{moved}} value(s).
array.notFound: {{x}} is not in the list: all {{checks}} values were checked.

dynamic.start: Size {{size}}, capacity {{capacity}}: {{spare}} spare slot(s) ready for appends.
dynamic.full: Full: size {{size}} = capacity {{capacity}}. Grow before appending.
dynamic.allocate: Allocate a new block with {{capacity}} slots, twice as big.
dynamic.copy: Copy slots[{{i}}] = {{value}} into the new block.
dynamic.switch: Switch to the new block (capacity {{capacity}}). The old one is freed.
dynamic.popEmpty: IndexError: pop from an empty list.
dynamic.pop: Remove the last value {{x}}. Size {{size}}, capacity stays {{capacity}}.
dynamic.end: {{appends}} append(s) needed {{copies}} copy step(s) in total: on average about one per append.

singly.help: insert x after y, add-first x, delete x, find x
singly.start: head → {{list}}. Each node holds a value and an arrow to the next node.
singly.walkMiss: Node {{value}}: not {{x}}, follow the arrow to the next node.
singly.createFirst: Create node {{x}} pointing at the old head, {{next}}.
singly.linkHead: Make {{x}} the new head: {{list}}. No other node moved.
singly.afterMissing: {{y}} is not in the list, so there is nothing to insert after.
singly.create: Create node {{x}} and point it at {{next}}.
singly.link: Point {{y}} at {{x}}: {{list}}. Only two arrows changed.
singly.emptyList: The list is empty: there is no {{x}}.
singly.findMiss: Reached None: {{x}} is not in the list ({{steps}} node(s) visited).
singly.headMatch: The head is {{x}}, so the new head is the node after it.
singly.prevStart: Start with prev at the head, {{value}}. Look for {{x}} one node ahead.
singly.prevMove: The next node isn't {{x}}: move prev to {{value}}.
singly.deleteMissing: Reached the end: {{x}} is not in the list.
singly.found: The node after {{prev}} is {{x}}: unlink it.

doubly.help: add-first x, add-last x, delete x
doubly.start: head ⇄ {{list}}. Each node points both to the next node and back to the previous one.
doubly.linkEmpty: The list was empty, so {{x}} is both the head and the tail.
doubly.deleteFind: Start from node {{x}}: it knows both its neighbours.
doubly.noPrev: {{x}} has no previous node: it was the head. The new head is {{next}}.
doubly.noNext: {{x}} had no next node: it was the tail. The new tail is {{prev}}: {{list}}.

stack.start: items = {{list}}. Only the top can be touched.
stack.push: Push {{x}} on top. The stack holds {{size}} value(s).
stack.pop: Pop the top value {{x}}. Now items = {{list}}.
stack.peek: Peek: the top is {{x}}, and it stays there.
stack.popEmpty: IndexError: pop from an empty stack.
stack.peekEmpty: IndexError: nothing to peek at, the stack is empty.

queue.start: items = {{list}}. Values join at the back and leave from the front.
queue.enqueue: Enqueue {{x}} at the back. The queue holds {{size}} value(s).
queue.dequeue: Dequeue: {{x}} leaves from the front. Now items = {{list}}.
queue.front: Front: {{x}} is next in line, and it stays there.
queue.dequeueEmpty: IndexError: pop from an empty deque.

deque.help: push_back x, push_front x, pop_back, pop_front
deque.start: d = deque({{list}}). Values can join or leave at either end.

ring.start: A ring of {{capacity}} slots. head marks the front; the tail is head + size, wrapped around.
ring.tailWrap: tail = (head {{head}} + size {{size}}) % {{capacity}} = {{tail}}: it wraps around to the start.
ring.full: OverflowError: all {{capacity}} slots are full, so {{x}} can't join.
ring.read: Read the front value {{x}} from slot {{head}}.
ring.advance: Clear the slot and move head to {{head}}. Size {{size}}.
ring.advanceWrap: Clear the slot and move head to {{head}}: it wraps around. Size {{size}}.
ring.empty: IndexError: the ring buffer is empty.
ring.end: Done: {{size}} of {{capacity}} slots in use. No value was ever moved.

binary.start: Look for {{target}} in a sorted list of {{count}} values.
binary.init: Start with the whole list: lo = {{lo}}, hi = {{hi}}.
binary.loop: lo {{lo}} ≤ hi {{hi}}: the target could still be at index {{lo}}..{{hi}}.
binary.goRight: {{value}} < {{target}}, so {{target}} can only be to the right. Discard the left half: lo = {{lo}}.
binary.goLeft: {{value}} > {{target}}, so {{target}} can only be to the left. Discard the right half: hi = {{hi}}.
binary.empty: lo {{lo}} > hi {{hi}}: nothing is left to search.
binary.notFound: {{target}} is not in the list. Return -1. Comparisons made: {{comparisons}}.

predict.title: Your prediction
predict.question: Will items[{{i}}] = {{value}} equal {{target}}?
predict.minQuestion: items[{{j}}] = {{a}}. Is it smaller than the smallest so far, {{b}}?
predict.shiftQuestion: items[{{j}}] = {{a}}. Is it bigger than the key {{key}}?
predict.mergeQuestion: Left has {{a}}, right has {{b}}. Which goes into the result next?

error.tooMany: Use at most {{max}} values. Small examples are easier to follow.
error.notInteger: Use whole numbers only, separated by commas.
error.targetMissing: Enter a target value to search for.
error.notSorted: Binary search needs the values in ascending order, for example 1, 3, 5, 7.
error.notDigits: Counting sort here uses small keys: whole numbers from 0 to 9.
error.negative: Radix sort here needs numbers from 0 to 99, with no negatives.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: There is nothing at {{path}}. It may have moved, or the link may be mistyped.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: This screen hit an unexpected error. Reloading usually fixes it.

pwa.updateAvailable: A new version of AlgoVerse is available.
pwa.offlineReady: AlgoVerse is ready to work offline.
